# Lockheed vs. RTX: who leads the missile market as budgets shift to munitions

Defense News, May 20, 2026

Lockheed Martin and RTX dominate U.S. missile procurement, together accounting for the majority of Army and Navy munitions spending in the fiscal 2026 budget request. Lockheed leads in interceptors (PAC-3 MSE, THAAD) and long-range fires (GMLRS, PrSM, HIMARS launchers), while RTX leads in air-to-air missiles (AIM-120 AMRAAM, AIM-9X) and the Standard Missile family.

Northrop Grumman and Boeing are smaller players in munitions but larger in strategic programs: Northrop on the Sentinel ICBM and B-21, Boeing on the F-15EX and KC-46. General Dynamics is the leading supplier of ordnance and shipbuilding.

The article's authors argue that Lockheed's moat is program incumbency: the F-35, Aegis and PAC-3 franchises have decades of planned sustainment, which analysts cited as the main reason Lockheed trades at a premium to General Dynamics and Northrop Grumman.
